summary: Initial discovery with Hydra Data Labs on dedicated inference needs. Customer runs mix of low-latency chat and batch reranking; primary concerns are tenant isolation, predictable p95 latency during marketing-driven surges, and integration with their key management. Redwood AE/SE walked through dedicated pool sizing, prewarm/hotpool options, and fallback routes to hosted models. Action: pricing, benchmark plan, and security artifacts to follow.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-22
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Hydra Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Hydra Platform Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Hydra Security), Kenji Ito (Hydra SRE)

Auto-Summary: quick notes captured by ff.ai - see next steps and action items

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava, I'm the AE on the account. We'll do a quick intro and then Daniel will take us through some of the dedicated options and how we handle surges.
[00:10] Priya: Thanks, Ava. Quick context — we run Hydra Chat, which is real-time, 100ms-ish target for single-turn responses, and we also have a batch rerank job overnight. Lately marketing promos have caused spikes up to 8x baseline for short windows.
[00:25] Daniel: Got it. Today we want to understand your tenancy preferences — are you leaning to full private/VPC, or dedicated pools with isolation? Also what's your SLA and burst tolerance.
[00:39] Marcus: For now we want Dedicated — mainly for tenancy isolation. We can't have noisy neighbor interference. But we'd like to avoid full private deployment due to ops burden.
[00:51] Sofia: Security is also key — KMS integration for in-flight or at-rest? Both. SOC2 is baseline, and we have some stricter audit log retention requirements for PRD data.
[01:04] Ava: Totally. We support KMS integrations and audit logs in Dedicated and Private. Daniel, quick note about eviction and prewarm.
[01:12] Daniel: Right. Two approaches: reserved prewarmed pools (hotpool) and burst-on-demand which can use reserved GPUs plus elastic burst or fallback to hosted variants. Prewarm gives lowest cold-start latency but costs more. Burst reduces cost but may add 200-600ms at peak if capacity needs to spin up, depending on model and quantization.
[01:30] Priya: The 200-600ms could be problematic for chat. Our p95 target is 150ms end-to-end.
[01:38] Daniel: For that we recommend a hotpool sized for 95th percentile steady-state with headroom for small bursts, plus a fast fallback policy to a lower-latency quantized model on the same GPU family. Also KV cache warmup can cut generation time significantly.
[01:52] Marcus: How do you calculate hotpool sizing? We have weird diurnal patterns and event-driven spikes.
[02:00] Daniel: We take your QPS distribution (per-minute), average token length, and desired p95 to simulate throughput. We also consider batching windows — aggressive batching reduces GPU ops but increases latency.
[02:15] Priya: We can share a 2-week request trace. It has microbursts during promo emails.
[02:21] Ava: Perfect. That's one of the action items — Priya, if you can share the trace, Daniel will run a sizing sim.
[02:30] Kenji: A question on isolation: we require node-level tenancy, so no co-tenancy with external customers. Does dedicated guarantee physical node isolation?
[02:40] Daniel: Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools — you can get node-level isolation or tenant pools mapped to dedicated nodes. For stricter needs we offer physical segregation and dedicated control plane options as part of Private. There's also RBAC and per-tenant network ACLs in VPC mode.
[02:56] Sofia: And about data retention and logging — can we route logs to our SIEM? We need immutable audit trails for model inputs/outputs for a subset of calls.
[03:07] Ava: Yes, you can forward logs to your SIEM and set retention. For sensitive payloads we support masking and selective redaction; note that retaining raw inputs is a compliance decision. We'll include security docs.
[03:22] Priya: Another thing — our batch rerank can be re-timed to off-peak but sometimes marketing requires near-real-time reranking for campaigns. How does Dedicated handle mixed workloads?
[03:33] Daniel: You can have segregated pools for real-time and batch. Batching jobs can be scheduled on lower-priority nodes or throttled. We also have dynamic scaling policies with burst quotas so batch jobs don't starve chat pools.
[03:46] Marcus: What happens if the burst exceeds reserved burst quotas? Is there graceful degradation or will we see errors?
[03:53] Daniel: We support multiple fallbacks — automatic routing to lower-cost model variants, draining non-critical requests, or redirecting to hosted capacity if allowed by policy. There's also a rate-limiting guardrail to avoid total service outage.
[04:10] Priya: That hosting fallback — do we lose data residency guarantees?
[04:15] Ava: If you allow hosted fallback, requests routed to hosted may leave your dedicated nodes; we can restrict fallbacks to specific regions to preserve residency but it's a policy tradeoff.
[04:27] Kenji: Latency profiling — can we get token-level traces?
[04:31] Daniel: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-token cost, latency breakdowns, and tracing hooks you can integrate into your observability stack. However, sampling level and retention are configurable.
[04:45] Sofia: In terms of encryption, we use an internal HSM. Does Redwood integrate with external HSMs or KMS?
[04:52] Daniel: We have KMS integrations with major cloud KMS providers and can support customer-managed keys in Private. For Dedicated we can integrate key wrapping through your KMS — we'll include specifics in the security whitepaper.
[05:05] Priya: Let's talk numbers — baseline QPS is 120RPS, promos spike to 1k RPS for 5-15 minutes. Typical response size is ~350 tokens for the chat flows.
[05:18] Daniel: Okay, that helps. Do you have percentiles for token lengths and the mix between chat and rerank?
[05:24] Priya: Chat is about 70% of latency-sensitive traffic, rerank is 20%, the rest are embeddings and housekeeping calls. Token length p50 140, p95 420.
[05:35] Marcus: Any recommendations for quantization? We want to preserve generation quality for chat but could accept minor degradation on rerank.
[05:43] Daniel: Use mixed profiles — FP16 or int8 quantization for batch/rerank models, maintain FP16 or bf16 with KV caching for chat models. Redwood Optimize can run offline evals on a prompt set to estimate quality delta.
[05:58] Priya: Are there any limits to switching model profiles during a surge? Like can we auto-fall back to quantized variant under load?
[06:05] Daniel: Yes — you can set policy-based fallbacks by route and by model. There's a small window where cache warming and KV cache incompatibilities can add latency; we recommend keeping quantized variants warmed or prewarmed in the hotpool if you plan to fallback rapidly.
[06:20] Ava: Quick interjection — we also offer scheduled prewarp? (prewarm) for anticipated events. You can ring-fence extra GPUs for promotional windows and prewarm them 15-30 minutes before the event to eliminate cold-starts.
[06:35] Marcus: How do prewarms affect billing? Do we pay for prewarm time?
[06:39] Ava: Yes, prewarm resources are billed like reserved capacity. There's also a burst credit model where you commit monthly baseline and use credits for spikes. We'll detail pricing but typical customers combine a committed baseline plus burst credits.
[06:54] Priya: On monitoring — we need per-route SLIs and alerts tied to model version rollouts. Can Redwood tie regression alerts to prompt sets?
[07:03] Daniel: Absolutely. We support eval-driven quality monitoring; you can attach test prompt sets and get regression alerts on BLEU/EMB/LLS metrics and also custom checks for hallucinations.
[07:17] Speaker 1: [inaudible]...
[07:20] Kenji: A SRE-specific: how is node maintenance handled? If a GPU node goes down during a big promo, what's the failover behavior?
[07:28] Daniel: We have proactive health checks and can failover traffic to other nodes or to dedicated warm standby pools. If loss is sudden, autoscaling can bring up additional nodes but that takes time — hence the recommendation for hotpool headroom for critical chat.
[07:45] Priya: What's the typical failover time to a hot standby?
[07:49] Daniel: If already warmed, routing changes are sub-200ms. If we need to spin new instances, that can be 20-90s depending on model size and image load times.
[08:01] Marcus: For our compliance folks, will audit logs include the routing decision metadata (which model, which node)?
[08:07] Ava: Yes, logs include model id, node id, latency, and routing policy decision metadata; you can ship them to your SIEM.
[08:16] Sofia: We also need SSO integration and RBAC for different teams.
[08:20] Daniel: SSO/SAML and granular RBAC are supported. You can create teams with scoped permissions for deploys, rollouts, and access to logs.
[08:32] Priya: Two small edge cases: 1) prompt injection detection at the routing layer; 2) handling of PII in logs for retraining.
[08:41] Daniel: We have optional middleware for prompt sanitization and an event-based scrubber for logs. For training data retention, we recommend explicit opt-ins with masking. We'll share the security playbook.
[08:55] Ava: I'm going to pause and check — are we aligned that Hydra wants Dedicated with node-level isolation and an initial hotpool sized for p95 with reserved burst credits?
[09:05] Priya: Yes, but we want a proposal that shows cost tradeoffs for hotpool-only, hotpool+burst credits, and a private option.
[09:14] Marcus: And show expected p95 for each scenario.
[09:17] Daniel: We'll simulate with your traces. One caveat: if you require physical node-level exclusivity for certain datasets, that pushes toward Private, but we can often satisfy with Dedicated isolated pools.
[09:30] Kenji: Any special network requirements? We use internal VPC peering and strict egress rules.
[09:36] Ava: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private networking; for Private we can offer a customer-managed control plane. We'll capture the exact CIDR needs in the technical deep dive.
[09:48] Speaker 2: [crosstalk] sorry dropped for a sec
[09:51] Priya: No worries. Also, can Redwood do blue/green model rollouts? We want to test new model versions on 5% of traffic.
[09:58] Daniel: Yes — rollouts, canary, and A/B tests are first-class. You can route by percent or by token-level hooks. Rollbacks are automatic on regression alerts if you enable automated rollback.
[10:12] Marcus: For the burst model variants — do we maintain separate KV caches per model or can caches be shared for fast fallback?
[10:19] Daniel: Caches are model-specific; however, we can warm cross-compatible variants if architecture allows. Sharing across quantized vs non-quantized typically isn't compatible. That's why we recommend prewarming fallback models when low-latency fallback is required.
[10:34] Priya: Are there tooling SDKs for instrumentation? We want lightweight hooks to tag requests and trace across our stacks.
[10:40] Ava: Yes, SDKs include tracing hooks and you can pass metadata headers. We'll include integration examples in the docs.
[10:49] Daniel: Also note token-level cost metrics will show up so you can correlate cost per route.
[10:55] Kenji: On the ops side, what's the expected uplift to our SRE team if we go Dedicated vs Private?
[11:01] Marcus: Yeah, we want to avoid a 1:1 ops burden.
[11:05] Daniel: Dedicated reduces operational surface vs Private — Redwood handles the serving runtime, autoscaling, and kernel selection. Private requires more customer ops for control plane and networking. We can quantify expected hours in the proposal.
[11:18] Priya: For the benchmark plan — can you include latencies for a small, medium, and large model family? We use Llama2-ish and a custom fine-tuned variant.
[11:27] Daniel: We'll include 7b, 13b, and 70b-ish profiles in the sim and show p50/p95/p99 under your trace.
[11:35] Ava: Quick check — any regulatory constraints for data residency?
[11:38] Priya: We need EU residency for EU customer data and US for US data. Also some APAC data needs to stay in region.
[11:45] Daniel: We can partition by region and route based on policy; Dedicated pools can be region pinned.
[11:53] Sofia: One more from security: we need a copy of Redwood's penetration test reports and SOC2 Type II attestation.
[11:59] Ava: We'll attach those to the package.
[12:03] Marcus: Regarding billing, can we get visibility into per-token and per-route cost during the pilot?
[12:09] Ava: Yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost; you can generate route-specific billing exports. For pilot we'll enable detailed telemetry.
[12:18] Priya: We also want a trial — can you provide a short POC with reserved baseline for two weeks and simulated spike to validate our policies?
[12:26] Daniel: Yes — we typically do a two-week pilot with a small reserved baseline and a burst window. We'll run joint load tests.
[12:33] Kenji: For the joint tests, can we use our synthetic harness?
[12:37] Daniel: Absolutely. We can run the harness from your VPC and also from Redwood test agents to simulate mixed origins.
[12:44] Ava: All right — let me capture the commitments: Ava will send pricing, Daniel will send benchmark plan and sample sim, Priya will share traces and prompt set, Sofia will share security requirements. We'll schedule a technical deep dive week of Nov 2.
[12:58] Priya: That works. One small note — please call out any per-GPU limits and disk IO considerations for large prompt contexts.
[13:06] Daniel: We'll include kernel selection notes and recommended instance types and NVMe configs.
[13:14] Marcus: Also note our preference for 2x A100-equivalent GPUs per node for memory reasons.
[13:20] Daniel: Noted.
[13:23] Speaker 3: [inaudible]
[13:25] Ava: Any final questions?
[13:28] Priya: No, thank you. This is helpful.
[13:31] Sofia: Thanks. We'll look for the security pack.
[13:34] Ava: Great — we'll follow up with the package and schedule the deep dive. Thanks everyone.
